title: Positive-support probability estimate
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces: each coordinate space has strictly positive weights summing to one. For a real-valued function $g$ on the product space, suppose its expectation is zero and its second moment is positive. If $C>0$ and $\|g\|_{2,P}\le C\|g\|_{1,P}$, then $\frac{1}{4C^2}\le \Pr_P(g>0)$.
hypotheses_covered: Every coordinate weight is strictly positive and the weights in each coordinate sum to one
$g$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
The second moment of $g$ is positive
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and let $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have mean zero and positive second moment. If $C>0$ and $\|g\|_{2,P}\le C\|g\|_{1,P}$, then $1/(4C^2)\le\Pr_P(g>0)$.
